must_fix: Frontmatter date collision (mechanically verifiable, not currently caught by any checker in semiskill/authoring). dv-uvm-agent-checker's `semiskill-review-by: 2027-04-14` (line 14) is byte-for-byte identical to six other skills in this wave: dv-coverage-hole-disposition, dv-isa-step-compare, dv-protocol-checker-rule, dv-vip-release-compat, dv-status-rollup, and dv-config-space-coverage. This directly violates the frontmatter rule 'a date 6-14 months out; STAGGER it, do not reuse a sibling's.' Since no automated rule in semiskill/authoring (lint.py, consistency.py) currently checks this, it will not be caught before publish unless a human/reviewer does it — pick a distinct date in the 6-14-month window for each of the seven files.

Step 8 (lines 210-223) should be reworded so its title and 'Then place the files' sentence stop implying the agent writes to the filelist, and instead explicitly hand off the actual edit to the engineer the way step 4 already does for elaboration and the way step 8's own compile sentence already does for the build — otherwise the step contradicts the skill's line-32 promise that it never writes into the tree.
technical_errors: LOW CONFIDENCE (≈35, not a clear error). The clocking-block gotcha (lines 263-266: 'A driver on the clocking block with a monitor on the raw signals disagrees by one cycle. A clocking block samples its inputs a skew before the edge; a plain sample sees the value after the non-blocking update lands.') describes the well-known clocking-block-vs-raw-signal skew mismatch, but the mechanism as phrased ('samples its inputs a skew before the edge') describes clocking-block INPUT skew, which is the monitor-reads-through-a-clocking-block case, not the stated scenario (driver drives via clocking block, monitor reads raw signals). The conclusion — pick one sampling discipline for both sides and record which — is sound regardless, so this is imprecision in the explanation rather than wrong advice; not confident enough to call it a hard defect.

No other domain errors of substance found. The UVM handshake, reset, out-of-order, drain-check, analysis-port-is-a-function, and field-automation gotchas are all standard, correctly stated verification knowledge, and the register/RAL material is correctly kept out of scope (routed to dv-ral-bringup instead of being re-derived here).
verb_honesty: HIGH CONFIDENCE (≈85). Step 8's title (line 210: "### 8. Place coverage, then add the files to the build") and its body (line 216: "Then place the files. Read the profile's Filelist convention ... then Glob the filelist entry point and Grep it once for a reference agent's package to find the position your new package must take relative to it.") directly contradict the skill's own opening promise at line 32 ("it does not write into your tree — it drafts bodies into the reply for you to place"). The agent has only Read/Grep/Glob; it cannot 'place' or 'add' files to a filelist. What the step's tool use actually accomplishes is determining the POSITION a new package must occupy — but unlike step 4 (line 157-159) and step 8's own next paragraph (line 222-223, "Handoff: ask the engineer to compile the new package..."), there is no explicit handoff sentence telling the engineer to make the filelist edit at that position. Fix: retitle to something like 'Work out where coverage and the new files belong' and add a handoff line ('ask the engineer to add the package at that position and give you the filelist diff or build log') so the step matches the tool-only reality.

MODERATE CONFIDENCE (≈65). Step 5's title (line 161: "### 5. Connect the agent the way this environment already connects agents") overclaims the same way, though more softly — the body itself is careful ('Draft every get with its return value checked ... and say in the contract that you did', lines 169-170), so a careful reader recovers the truth from the body. Still, a bare imperative title ('Connect the agent') for a step that only Reads/Greps and drafts text is the same category of overclaim as step 8's, just less consequential.
hallucination_risks: LOW-MODERATE CONFIDENCE (≈40, below the normal bar, included for completeness). Step 5's config_db gotcha ('A set written with a wildcard scope and a get written with an exact one is the most common wiring failure ... the get returns zero, the handle keeps its default, and the first access is a fatal naming the component rather than the key', lines 166-169) is generically true UVM behaviour but states a specific directionality (set=wildcard, get=exact) for the mismatch as if it were the canonical failure shape. In practice the mismatch is symmetric (either side can be the mis-scoped one) and it isn't a house-specific fact, so it is defensible generic guidance rather than an invented convention — flagged only because it reads more specific than the evidence (no Grep/Read cited) supports.

No other invented tool flags, message strings, file names, class/macro names, or house conventions were found outside declared [[FILL:]] slots — this is a genuinely disciplined draft on this axis. Every base class, config key, port name, checker placement, and prediction source is correctly deferred to a slot rather than asserted.
budget_violations: Budget arithmetic checked line-by-line and found fully self-consistent: declared caps are 4 Globs / 14 Greps / 10 windowed Reads (line 78-81), and every step's actual Glob/Grep/Read count in the procedure text sums to exactly that (Globs: step1=2 + step3=1 + step8=1 = 4; Greps: 2+2+1+2+2+2+1+2 = 14; Reads: step2=4 + step4=2 + step5=1 + step6≤2 + step9-spare=1 = 10). This is unusually tight for a batch-generated skill and I could not find a step that silently exceeds its allocation.

SOFT NOTE, not a confirmed violation (≈35 confidence). Steps 4, 6 and 8 each achieve 'Grep both [reference agent] directories for X — one Grep' by implicitly assuming a single Grep call can be rooted at a shared parent directory covering both siblings (e.g. lines 144-146, 190-192, 212-213). If the two reference agents named in the 'Reference agents' slot do not share a scoped-enough common parent — or the pattern is generic enough to also match unrelated sibling agents under that parent — each of those 'two Greps' silently becomes four, which would blow the 14-Grep total. The skill never states this assumption, so it is worth a reviewer's eye rather than a rewrite.
review.open_twice: Yes, on balance. The retrieval budget's arithmetic is airtight and verified exactly against every step's stated tool allocation; the Gotchas section is dense with correct, non-invented, genuinely hard-won UVM knowledge (config_db wildcard scope mismatch, clocking-block-vs-raw-signal skew, analysis-write-is-a-function, field-automation over-comparison, active/passive monitor construction); the slot table is well justified against _shared/team-profile.md including a careful, rule-8-compliant explanation of how 'Acceptance gate' narrows 'Sign-off'; and every sibling-skill cross-reference in 'When to use something else' resolves to a real file. The one real content defect — step 8's 'place the files'/'add the files to the build' language contradicting the skill's own no-write promise — is a local, one-step wording problem, not a trust-destroying one, and the review-by date collision is a publish-metadata bug rather than a content bug. Neither is the kind of invented-fact problem that makes a senior engineer close the file and never reopen it.

recheck.why: Lint is 1.000 and clean, role/level are exactly ip-dv-engineer/intermediate, all 8 slots are spent, the budget arithmetic is exact (4 Globs / 14 Greps / 10 Reads, and the 14+5=19 paired-Grep contingency is right), every handoff field has an assigning step and none collides with a T1 enum or T3 held noun, and the DV content is strong — the clocking-block skew gotcha is correct in both directions. But two steps are structurally broken. Step 5 violates the skill's own bolded budget item 2 ("Never open a testbench file with Read first") by Reading the environment file before Grepping it, and the environment file is the only Read target in the skill that is neither Globbed nor Grepped for — all 4 Globs and step 5's 2 Greps are allocated elsewhere, so the one ~80-line window is chosen blind with no Read left to anchor afterwards. Step 6 offers no branch for three of the four placements its own Checker placement slot enumerates: its two Reads and two Greps are pinned to the two reference agent directories (budget item 4 says so verbatim), so an environment-level scoreboard, checks inside the monitor, or a reference model leaves the step with no retrieval target at all. Step 7 branches cleanly across all four of its cases; step 6 branches across none. Both are cheap to fix, which is what makes them defects rather than tradeoffs. This is a "nearly", and nearly is a no.
remaining: BLOCKER — step 5 contradicts the skill's own retrieval discipline. Budget item 2 reads 'Never open a testbench file with Read first. Glob to locate, Grep for a line number, then Read a bounded window around it.' Step 5 reads 'Read the environment file that builds a reference agent, then Grep it twice against the Connection convention slot: once for the key strings, once for the calls that consume them.' The environment file is the only Read target in the skill neither Globbed nor Grepped for beforehand (the 4 Globs go to the two agent paths, the interface file and the filelist entry point), and step 5's two Greps are already committed, so the single ~80-line window into the largest file in the testbench is chosen blind and no Read remains to window around the Grep hits. The golden reference dv-ral-bringup states the opposite rule and obeys it ('each entered through a Grep for the exact policy string or resource name, never by browsing'). Fix: swap the clauses so the Greps run first and the Read windows the hits.

BLOCKER — step 6 has no branch for three of the four placements its own slot enumerates. The Checker placement slot offers 'one scoreboard per agent, one environment-level scoreboard, checks inside the monitor, or a reference model'. Step 6 says 'Only then Read one sibling scoreboard, Grep both directories for the subscriber idiom and for the reporting method ... and Read the second scoreboard if the reporting idiom is still ambiguous', and budget item 4 pins those Greps as 'Grep both reference agent directories'. Under an environment-level scoreboard, checks-inside-the-monitor, or a reference model there is no scoreboard in either agent directory, so both Reads and both Greps have no target and the step offers no alternative path. Step 7 handles all four of its Prediction source cases explicitly; step 6 must do the same for Checker placement (and say where the Greps are scoped when the checker lives outside the agent directories, since that also moves the shared-parent argument in budget item 4).

MINOR — technically wrong clause in step 8: 'Sampling a covergroup in the monitor and again in a subscriber double-counts every bin, and the number looks better for it.' The double-count is right, the consequence is not: with option.at_least at its LRM default of 1, sampling the same item twice inflates hit counts and leaves the coverage percentage unchanged. The claim only holds where the team has raised at_least. Either qualify it or restate the real hazard — inflated hit counts hide how rare a bin actually is.
